# scribl timeline and milestones

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | draft for team review |


The backlog answers what and how much. This page answers when. It lays the
same work against the confirmed calendar. It adds no scope and changes no
feature size.

## The calendar

Source: `docs/meetings/schedule-plan.html`, lines 359 to 371. This calendar
already exists and is confirmed on 2026-08-20; it is not being invented here.

| Phase | Dates | Working days |
|---|---|---|
| Shape (discovery) | Monday 2026-08-24 to Tuesday 2026-09-01 | 7 |
| Sprint 1 | Wednesday 2026-09-02 to Tuesday 2026-09-15 | 10 |
| Sprint 2 | Wednesday 2026-09-16 to Tuesday 2026-09-29 | 10 |
| Sprint 3 | Wednesday 2026-09-30 to Tuesday 2026-10-13 | 10 |

Demo Wednesdays: 2026-09-02 (Shape readout), 2026-09-16, 2026-09-30, 2026-10-14.
The eight weeks end 2026-10-16. The last demo is 2026-10-14, so two working
days sit after it and there is no hardening sprint.

Sprint boundaries fall on Wednesdays, so a week-numbered grid is approximate
at every boundary. That holds true wherever weeks are used as labels below.

**The correction the backlog has to carry.** The backlog intro says "two weeks
of discovery." The confirmed calendar gives Shape seven working days, not ten:
the schedule plan says it costs Shape three working days to start sprint 1 on
2026-09-02 rather than 2026-09-09, and the later start would push the last
demo past the end of the eight weeks and into the re:Invent freeze around
2026-10-23. Discovery supply is seven days per full-time lane. The build
lanes get 20 discovery lane-days (Neelesh 2 at 30 percent, Nitish 7, Karuna 7,
Pankaj 4 at 0.6), not the 35 a full two weeks would give. Shubhankar Bhavsar is
onboarding through this window and carries no build days in it.

## What discovery produces

The backlog previously assigned discovery output only to QA and to decisions.
It never said what the iOS and backend lanes build. This is that answer.
Every item is real backlog work pulled forward, so every day spent here comes
off a build sprint.

### Neelesh Aggarwal, iOS, 7 days

| Item | Days | Week | Depends on an open question |
|---|---|---|---|
| E01-F9 app shell, routing and the single brand theme, whole feature | 5 | Shell and routing in week 1, the theme pass in week 2 | Q1, Q3, Q4. The shell and routing need no design answer. The theme pass needs the tokens out of the design working session on 2026-08-26 and the design sync on 2026-08-27. If those slip, the theme half slips into sprint 1 and 2 iOS-days come back onto the sprint 1 queue |
| E04-F1 Skia canvas, the first 2 of its 5 days | 2 | Week 2 | Q1, Q2. The canvas engine work, the Skia surface, stroke capture and undo, is ink-agnostic, so it can start before the six inks are named. The ink palette itself waits on Q1 and Q2 |

Absorbs 7 of the 41 green iOS-days. The iOS build-sprint demand drops to 34
against 30.

### Nitish Goyal, backend, 7 days

| Item | Days | Week | Depends on an open question |
|---|---|---|---|
| E01-F5 API contract and mock server, whole feature | 2 | Week 1 | None. Needs no AWS account. This is the item that lets QA write API-level tests and iOS code against a stub, so it goes first |
| E01-F3 relational data model, the schema draft, 3 of its 4 days | 3 | Weeks 1 and 2 | None to draft. The schema and its migrations are authored and reviewed here; the remaining day applies them to a provisioned environment in sprint 1, which needs Q17 and Q49. E01-F3 formally depends on E01-F2, and Shape deliberately overrides that for the drafting half only, because authoring a schema needs no CDK stack. The dependency holds for the applied day, which is why it follows the deploy in sprint 1. |
| E01-F2 CDK stack skeleton, 2 of its 3 days | 2 | Week 2 | Q17, Q49. CDK can be authored and synthesized locally with no account. It cannot be deployed. The third day is the deploy, in sprint 1 |

Absorbs 7 of the 53 green backend-days.

### Pankaj Aggarwal, engineering lead and architect, 4 days at 0.6

| Item | Days | Week | Depends on an open question |
|---|---|---|---|
| E01-F1 AWS accounts and three environments | 2 | Weeks 1 and 2 | Q17, Q49. Blocked on both. What is doable regardless is the account request, the environment design and the cost shape. If Q17 and Q49 are still open on 2026-09-02, nothing deploys in sprint 1 and the whole backend lane stalls behind it |
| E07-F2 build host and pipeline decision | 1 | Week 1 | Q47. This feature is the decision, so Shape is exactly where it belongs |
| An auth and identity ADR | 1 | Week 2 | None |

The auth ADR is not a backlog feature today, and that is the gap. No ADR
covers auth or identity anywhere, while E02-F1 recommends a Cognito user pool
and every authorization check in E04 and E05 reads the identity it issues.
One page from Pankaj in Shape closes it. It should become a feature at sprint
1 planning rather than staying an unlisted deliverable.

Pankaj's 2 days on E01-F1 absorb 2 more of the 53 green backend-days, so the
backend lane absorbs 9 in total and its build-sprint demand drops to 44
against 39.

### Karuna Arshakota, QA, 7 days

| Item | Days | Week |
|---|---|---|
| E06-F1 QA process standard for this engagement | 3 | Week 1 |
| E06-F2 tooling recommendation with the alternatives written down | 4 | Weeks 1 and 2 |

E06-F4, requirements review and traceability, is not in Shape. It was
double-booked, appearing both in the discovery fill and in Karuna's sprint 1
lane. It sits in sprint 1 only, which is also where its blockers resolve. It is gated on Q15 and Q16, the design questions Shape exists to answer.

Absorbs 7 of the 24 green QA-days, so QA build-sprint demand is 17 against
30. That grows QA slack from 6 days to 13. Those 13 days are the entire
test-execution budget for the app across three sprints and nothing else in
the plan funds execution, so they are that budget rather than slack.

### Pramod Kumar, delivery, 3 days at 0.4

E07-F1, chasing the Apple Developer account (Q5) daily until it closes.
E07-F4, the TestFlight distribution process written for Scribl. The answers
to Q44 through Q48. The roster holiday calendar named above. All unsized
coordination work.

### What the discovery allocation buys

Green build-lane demand is 128 against 108. Shape absorbs 18 green lane-days
(2 iOS, 9 backend and 7 QA), which takes green demand to 110 against 108.

It does not close the overrun per lane, and the lane rows are the ones that
matter because an idle QA-day cannot be spent as an iOS-day. After Shape, iOS is 41
against 39, still 2 over. Backend is 51 against 39, still 12 over. QA is 17
against 30, 13 under. The fourteen remaining lane-days of overrun sit in the two
lanes with no slack, and face 13 days of slack in the lane that cannot
convert.

Shape is the cheapest relief available, and it was worth claiming before
asking for money. It is not a fix. The green band still does not fit in the
two lanes that build the product.

## Milestones

Bar the Shape readout, every date here is a demo Wednesday off the confirmed
calendar. The "not yet true" column is the one a client reads.

### M0, Shape readout, Wednesday 2026-09-02

True: the dated calendar and the sprint 1 queue. The API contract and a
running mock server. The relational schema drafted and reviewed. The CDK
stack authored and synthesizing locally. The app shell running with routing
and the single brand theme. The Skia canvas engine started. The QA process
standard and the tooling recommendation. The build host and pipeline
decision. An auth and identity ADR.

Not yet true: nothing is deployed to AWS, because Q17 and Q49 decide whose
account and whose money. No signed build exists and nothing is in
TestFlight. Nobody outside the delivery team has touched anything. No
onboarding, no submit, no wall.

### M1, sprint 1 demo, Wednesday 2026-09-16. The anchor, end of week four

True: a hosted API and a relational database in a real AWS environment. Sign
in with email and password, on a device. Today's prompt on screen. The Skia
canvas with the six inks, and you can draw on it. A manually signed build in
TestFlight that named testers can install and open. In Rob's words: here is
the app, it is hosted, it has a back end, it is in TestFlight and you can use
it.

Not yet true, and this is the honest half. Submitting does not persist your
drawing. The submit endpoint needs presigned upload (E04-F4, 3 backend-days)
which needs media storage and delivery (E01-F6, 3 backend-days), and there
are not 6 spare backend-days in a lane committed to 10 of 10. So what you
draw is not saved and nothing unlocks a wall. Guided onboarding screens 1 to
8 are not built, so first run is bare. There are no walls, no channels and no
other people's work to see. There is no invite path, so a second person
cannot reach a wall. The build is signed by hand, not by CI. No push, no
streaks, no moderation, no analytics.

Two gates, not one. This milestone is conditional on both of them, and either
one alone takes most of the "true" column away.

Gate Q5, the Apple Developer account. If it has not closed by 2026-09-02,
E07-F1, E07-F3 and E07-F4 stall, there is no TestFlight build here, and the demo
is a screen recording rather than an app on a tester's phone.

Gate Q17 with Q49, whose AWS account and whose money. The hosted API and the
database in the "true" column are exactly as conditional as the TestFlight
build. Ranks 1 and 2 in the backend lane cannot start until these close, and
nothing else in that lane deploys behind them. If they are still open on
2026-09-02, "it is hosted, it has a back end" is not true at this demo, and what
survives is the app running against E01-F5's mock server.

### M2, sprint 2 demo, Wednesday 2026-09-30

True: guided onboarding, screens 1 to 8. Submit persists, with artwork in S3
behind CloudFront. Submit-to-unlock at the data layer, with its bypass test.
Today's prompt served from the seeded curated set on the real fetch contract
rather than the mock. An automated signed build out of CI. The QA automation
harness running against the contract.

Not yet true: walls and channels are backend-first, so the social half is not
demonstrable end to end. No reactions. No dashboard or stats card. Invites
are still unfunded (Q8). Still no push, streaks, moderation or analytics.

### M3, sprint 3 demo, Wednesday 2026-10-14

True: the daily loop end to end for one person and their wall. Prompt, draw,
submit, unlock, the wall grid and a response detail. Server-side channel
isolation with its regression gate. Crash reporting with build traceability.
The release gate applied at the demo rather than after it.

Not yet true: no daily nudge, no moderation lane, no streaks, no analytics
events. All four are orange band and none has a slot. No dashboard or stats
card if E05-F5 stays cut. No invite path, so a second person still reaches a
wall only by a route nobody has funded. Not submitted to the App Store, and
whether submission is even in this phase is Q56. No iPad.

The eight weeks end 2026-10-16, two working days after this demo. There is no
hardening sprint.

## The overrun, per lane

Reviewer's recomputed figures, confirmed against the backlog's own rollup.

| Lane | Supply | Green | Green load | Green plus orange | G+O load | After Shape | Load after Shape |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iOS, Neelesh Aggarwal | 30 | 41 | 137% | 50 | 167% | 34 | 113% |
| Backend and AWS, Nitish Goyal plus Pankaj Aggarwal | 39 | 53 | 136% | 80 | 205% | 44 | 113% |
| QA, Karuna Arshakota | 30 | 24 | 80% | 24 | 80% | 17 | 57% |
| Total build lanes | 99 | 118 | 119% | 154 | 156% | 95 | 96% |

The headline percentages are 137/167, 136/205 and 80/80, and the "after
Shape" column is the second set to read. The totals row is the rollup of the
three lanes shown, and earlier copies of the backlog totalled green at 119
and green plus orange at 155, both counting the one platform green-day twice
and both dividing by 105 rather than 99.

Read the lane rows, not the total. A 96 percent total load after Shape reads
as solved. It is not. An idle QA-day cannot be spent as an iOS-day, so the
two build lanes are still over while QA carries slack it cannot lend.
